name: Winjarumi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record winj1235 and reference record 70404; Grambank language page winj1235; Wikipedia 'Worrorra language'.
sources.note: Glottolog: 0 descriptive refs; MEDs = McGregor 2004 (phonology_or_text by page count only) and Capell & Coate 1984 (wordlist_or_less). Grambank sources: Capell & Coate 1984, McGregor 2004. Wikipedia lists Windjarumi among Worrorra dialects; no stress info.

sources.citation: Clendon, Mark. 2014. Worrorra: a language of the north-west Kimberley coast. Adelaide: University of Adelaide Press. doi 10.20851/worrorra.
sources.note: Proxy only (Worrorra proper, worr1237, already catalogued): sec. 2.6.2 'Timing' pp. 38-46 -- stress not phonemic; attracted to long vowels and to the penult; global/phrasal rhythm overrides. Contains no Winjarumi data and does not mention the variety's prosody.

sources.citation: McGregor, William B. & Alan Rumsey. 2009. Worrorran revisited: the case for genetic relations among languages of the Northern Kimberley region of Western Australia. Pacific Linguistics 600. Canberra: ANU. hdl 1885/50063.
sources.note: Table 1 p. 2: Winjarumi 'no surviving speakers'; Table 2 p. 4 (pdf p. 17): main source of data on Winjarumi = 'Capell and Coate (1984)' only. Ch. 4 (phonology, pp. 21ff.) gives a generic Worrorran segment inventory and discusses Unggumi vowels/lamino-dentals; no statement of stress placement for any variety (only an aside about mid vowels 'within initial stressed syllables' re Unggumi). Winjarumi cited only for a few lexical comparanda ('sit' ada, 'climb' bari, 'breast' nga(a)mugu, 'eye' yubulu, 'sun' marangunya, 'I' ngaya).

sources.citation: McGregor, William. 1988. Handbook of Kimberley languages, vol. 1: General information. Pacific Linguistics C-105. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Entry 5.6 Winjarumi/Windjarumi, pp. 94-95: 'People who have worked intensively on the language: No one'; 'Word lists: None'; 'Textual material: None'; 'Grammar or sketch grammar: None; Capell & Coate (1984) contains some information'; speakers: 'Presumably extinct. Capell & Coate (1984) - 1 speaker'. Bibliographic inventory only; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Capell, A. & H. H. J. Coate. 1984. Comparative studies in Northern Kimberley languages. Pacific Linguistics C-69. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: The only work containing primary Windjarumi data (Coate's notes from a single, last speaker; pp. vii, 3: material 'very limited, especially Windjarumi'; treated as a dialect of the Worora complex). Ch. 1 'Phonological principles' (pp. 7-17: phonemic systems, syllable, morphophonemics) has no stress/accent section at all. Windjarumi appears only in class-prefix/suffix tables, a handful of nouns (p. 70), the negator wa, and repeated notes that no material is available. Nothing on Windjarumi stress.
